analysis.title: Morning Market Tidbits: Change of Fed call: hikes in Dec '26 and Mar '27
key_insights: The Fed held rates at its October meeting. BofA still expects two more hikes but has moved them to a quarterly pace, Dec '26 and Mar '27.
BofA's terminal rate forecast stays at 4.25-4.5%, and it expects policy rates to stay there through end-2027. The change in timing has no material impact on BofA's macro forecasts.
Markets price over a 60% chance of hikes in Dec '26 and Mar '27.

Main risk to the new call: by moving slower the Fed could fall behind the curve. BofA would not rule out 25-50bp of additional hikes versus its base case in 2027, at consecutive meetings or a quarterly cadence.
Alternative scenario: y/y core PCE inflation rolls off significantly early next year on favorable base effects. In that case the Fed might stop after one more hike in Dec '26.
BofA's 3Q GDP tracking estimate is 3.5% q/q saar, down two-tenths after advance goods trade and wholesale inventories. Its official 3Q GDP forecast is 3.5%.

Today's data: 3Q GDP advance estimate and Sep PCE inflation, personal income and outlays. BofA expects GDP at 3.5% vs consensus 3.2%, and Sep core PCE at 0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y, in line with consensus.
The Fed blackout period ends today.

tension_points.bull_case: A slower quarterly pace of hikes is enough. If y/y core PCE rolls off significantly early next year on favorable base effects, the Fed could stop after one more hike in Dec '26 and its caution would be vindicated.
tension_points.bear_case: By moving slower the Fed could fall behind the curve, and BofA would not rule out 25-50bp of additional hikes relative to its base case in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Y/y core PCE inflation rolling off significantly early next year due to base effects would invalidate the need for the Mar '27 hike and beyond.
